subject: Draft: evaluation MAP, exit gates and acceptance tests for Novamed
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cruz <samantha@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP and acceptance checklist (first pass)

Samantha —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation milestones, the acceptance tests we propose for the pilot, and a suggested close timeline that maps to your procurement window. High-level asks:

- Review the objective alignment section (tab 1) to confirm the two primary success signals for the pilot: 1) 95th-percentile inference latency <= 250ms on standard flows; 2) production-quality intent/slot extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the annotated evaluation set.
- Confirm the acceptance test owners on your side (we've put Procurement + Dev Lead as approvers).
- Flag any compliance or evidence gaps — I attached the SOC2 evidence request spreadsheet we use for the private deploys.

Proposed timeline (short):
- Week 1: Data access & sandbox provisioning (Novamed provides sample dataset + access window)
- Week 2: Baseline metric collection (Redwood runs baseline against supplied sample data)
- Week 3: Pilot run + acceptance tests (we run N=3 evaluation runs, stability, latency, quality)
- Week 4: Close review and contract sign-off if acceptance is met.

I'm sharing a recording of today's demo in case you want to forward internally; the MAP includes explicit exit gates and rollback triggers so nothing is fuzzy. If this looks like a good starting point, I can convert to a mutual spreadsheet and lock owners.

Attachments: Novamed_MAP_v1.xlsx (excel), SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (pdf), demo-recording.mp4 (video link stub)

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi

From: Samantha Cruz <samantha@novamed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and acceptance checklist (first pass)

Thanks Irene — that looks useful. A few quick notes after a rapid skim:

- The latency target is reasonable but we'd like to see a tiered acceptance:
  * Tier A (must pass): p95 <= 300ms for critical paths (patient search, triage)
  * Tier B (stretch): p95 <= 250ms for non-critical advisory flows
- For quality F1, can you confirm how you plan to score intents vs slots? We need slot accuracy prioritized for certain clinical fields.
- Procurement wants to see how rollback would work from a data retention standpoint (e.g., KV cache flush, key deletion). They will need the SOC2 evidence packet filled out by Friday for legal to review.

I'll loop in our Procurement alias next. Also copying our Lead Engineer, Tom Willis, privately; he'll push any technical redlines to you directly if needed.

Samantha Cruz
Director of Product, Novamed Health
samantha@novamed.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cruz <samantha@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and acceptance checklist (first pass)

Samantha —

Great feedback, thanks. Quick responses inline: 

- Tiered latency: yes — I've updated the MAP (tab 2) to reflect a two-tier acceptance with explicit measurement windows and sample sizes (p95 computed over 10k user-simulated requests, two separate runs).
- Quality scoring: we will produce intent and slot F1 separately and an aggregated weighted score. For the pilot we recommend weighting slots at 0.6 and intents at 0.4 for the clinical flows you called out. We can make that configurable based on your priority list.
- Rollback/data controls: see SOC2-evidence-request.pdf and a new 'rollback playbook' section in the MAP. Short answer: KV cache flush and model routing rollback are atomic operations in our runtime; we will provide an ops playbook and a test to verify that no PII remains in transient caches within your retention SLA.

Next steps proposed:
- Novamed to confirm data access window by EOD Wed (17 Mar).
- Tom Willis (or another engineer) to send a list of dataset sample fields we should expect (schema).
- Procurement to confirm review timeline (target signoff 4/9).

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet to accept inline comments and will re-share a link to the Drive folder when ready. If Procurement needs any additional compliance artifacts, Marissa can pull the evidence pack.

Cheers,
Irene

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cruz <samantha@novamed.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance test details & verification plan

Samantha / Irene —

Adding a short technical walkthrough of the acceptance tests so Novamed's engineering team has a clear checklist to run or observe. This will be included as an acceptance appendix in the MAP. Key items: 

1) Latency/Throughput acceptance
  - Test harness: Redwood synthetic runner (10k requests, traffic mix file attached in MAP)
  - Measurement windows: 3 runs, 30-minute windows each, collect p50/p95/p99 and tails
  - Gate: Tier A pass requires p95 <= 300ms on critical endpoints in 2/3 runs.

2) Quality acceptance (intent/slot)
  - Dataset: Novamed annotated sample (min 1k labeled examples across critical intents)
  - Scoring: Intent F1, Slot F1, weighted score (slots=0.6)
  - Gate: Weighted score >= 0.88; individual slot F1 >= 0.82 for clinical fields.

3) Reliability & failover acceptance
  - Simulate instance failure and validate automated routing to fallback variant within 5s.
  - Gate: No data loss, and <1% failed requests during failover window.

4) Compliance evidence checklist
  - SOC2 snapshot, audit logs for evaluation window, key deletion confirmation log.

If Tom or Procurement want to run any of these locally we can provide the runner and an execution playbook; Connor will support to ingest Novamed's sample corpus into a sandbox (read-only).

Irene — I'll add these as acceptance tests in a locked tab and assign owners. Samantha — can you confirm who on your team will be the technical approver and who will sign the quality acceptance?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
